dimensions.detail: The skill purpose, documentation, and run.sh align: it wraps curl for fixed PrusaLink endpoints only: status, job, upload, start, and cancel.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The script can upload files and start or cancel printer jobs on the configured host, which is expected for this purpose and limited to user-provided commands rather than arbitrary API requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is a local folder copy with no package install, remote download, or runtime code execution beyond invoking the included shell script and curl.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: It requires a printer host and either Digest credentials or an API key, which is proportionate; however it defaults to HTTP, so credentials or API keys may be exposed on an untrusted network unless HTTPS is configured.
dimensions.label: Credentials

llm.findings: [SQP-2] expected: Verified: PRUSALINK_SCHEME defaults to http and authenticated curl requests can be sent over HTTP. This is a real transport-security caveat, but it is disclosed, configurable to HTTPS, limited to the configured PrusaLink host, and not evidence of hidden or purpose-mismatched behavior.
llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable letting the agent control the configured printer. Set PRUSALINK_HOST to a trusted local printer, prefer HTTPS if your printer supports it, and use --password-file or a secret store instead of putting credentials directly in commands.
llm.summary: This is a transparent PrusaLink printer-control wrapper with a real but disclosed HTTP transport caveat.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: prusalink-cli
Version: 1.0.2

The skill is a legitimate CLI wrapper for the PrusaLink API, providing basic 3D printer management functions like status checks and G-code uploads via curl. The implementation in run.sh is transparent, lacks obfuscation, and includes security-conscious features such as a --password-file option to prevent credential leakage in shell history. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection was found.
